discovery: Spin qubits in semiconductors: proposal and realization of quantum computation with single electron and nuclear spins in silicon and quantum dots

nominees.name: Bruce E. Kane
nominees.affiliation: Laboratory for Physical Sciences, University of Maryland, USA

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech, Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

motivation: In 1998 Loss (with DiVincenzo) proposed encoding qubits in single electron spins in quantum dots, and Kane proposed qubits in individual phosphorus donor spins in silicon. These two papers turned the semiconductor, the material of all modern electronics, into a platform for quantum computing. Vandersypen led the experimental realization: single-shot spin readout, coherent single-spin control, and high-fidelity two-qubit gates in silicon, which ultimately went beyond fault-tolerance thresholds. Together these advances showed that the quantum state of one electron or nucleus can be isolated, controlled and entangled inside a solid-state device. That opened a worldwide effort, in academia and industry, to build quantum processors compatible with CMOS manufacturing. The 2025 prize recognized macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits. The spin-qubit programme is the complementary, atomic-scale route, with deep physics and transformative technological reach.
